plant_color_index — SEGMENTATION plant op

• Data kinds: rgbimage → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.plant_color_index(rgb, *, index: 'str' = 'exg', dark_floor: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'Dict[str, object]' (to call the implementation directly, import cropweed; cropweed.plant_color_index(rgb, *, index: 'str' = 'exg', dark_floor: 'float' = 0.02) -> 'Dict[str, object]'; from the registry, opssegmentation.get("plant_color_index"))

Usage

Per-pixel plant colour indices from the three visible bands (ExG, ExR, ExGR, CIVE, NGRDI, VEG).

rgb is (H, W, 3). uint8 is divided by 255; float outside [0, 1] is refused. index is exg / exr / exgr / cive / ngrdi / veg. ExG, ExR, ExGR, CIVE and VEG use the chromatic coordinates r = R/(R+G+B), g, b; only NGRDI uses the raw (G − R)/(G + R). Pixels whose brightness (mean of RGB) is below dark_floor have chromaticity set by noise, so no value is made (NaN) and valid is False (VEG also drops pixels with r or b = 0, NGRDI those with G + R = 0).

Returns: index (H, W float, NaN = undefined), valid (bool), name, formula, vegetation_sign (+1 for indices that grow with plants, −1 for CIVE and ExR), citation, n_invalid, threshold_zero_is_boundary (True only for ExGR: 0 separates plant and background). Empty input, non-finite values, out-of-range values, unknown index names and images where every pixel is undefined raise ValueError.

Call example: fs.ledger.plant_color_index(img, index="exgr")["index"] > 0 gives the plant pixels.
